findings.title: DLQ path crashes for messages whose attributes are None or missing mapping semantics
findings.evidence: The retry-count helper tolerates bad attributes by returning 0, but the dead-letter send path later unconditionally expands message.attributes into a dict. If a supported queue implementation provides attributes as None, the first terminal failure reaches this line and raises before the message is acked or dead-lettered, causing an endless redelivery loop instead of dead-lettering.
findings.recommendation: Normalize attributes once before use, for example with 'attrs = dict(message.attributes or {})', and use that both in _delivery_attempts and in the dlq.send attributes payload.

findings.title: Successful handler execution is retried if ack fails, duplicating non-idempotent side effects
findings.evidence: After 'handler(message.body)' returns successfully, the code immediately calls ack without any error handling. On a reachable broker/network failure during ack, process_messages raises and exits after the handler has already performed its side effects, leaving the message unacked so it will be redelivered and processed again.
findings.recommendation: Handle ack failures explicitly after successful processing, e.g. catch exceptions around ack, log them, and decide on a strategy that avoids blind re-execution of non-idempotent handlers, such as requiring idempotency keys or persisting completion before ack.
